statement.p: Let \mathcal{S} be the square in the xy-plane shown in the figure below, oriented with the normal pointing in the positive z-direction. Estimate \iint_{\mathcal{S}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\mathbf{S} where \mathbf{F} is a vector field whose values at the labeled points are \begin{array}{llll} \mathbf{F}(A) \amp = \left\lt 6,-4,-7\right>,\amp \qquad \mathbf{F}(B) \amp = \left\lt 8,-1,2\right>\\ \mathbf{F}(C) \amp = \left\lt 4,-4,-3\right>,\amp \qquad \mathbf{F}(D) \amp = \left\lt -5,-6,2\right>\end{array}

image.shortdescription: A two by two grid of squares with center points of each square labeled A in the top left, B in the top right, C in the bottom left, and D in the bottom right.

description.p: A two by two grid of squares with center points of each square labeled A in the top left, B in the top right, C in the bottom left, and D in the bottom right.

static.solution:
S is = \left\lt 0,0,1\right>.
We estimate the vector surface integral \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} using the division and sample points given in the Figure.
Each subsquare has area \frac14, therefore we obtain the following estimation: \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} \approx \left(\mathbf{F} (A)\cdot {\mathbf{e}}_n + \mathbf{F} (B) \cdot {\mathbf{e}}_n +\mathbf{F} (C) \cdot {\mathbf{e}}_n + \mathbf{F} (D) \cdot {\mathbf{e}}_n\right) \cdot \frac14 = (\left\lt 6,-4,-7\right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,1\right>+\left\lt 8,-1,2\right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,1\right>+\left\lt 4,-4,-3\right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,1\right>+\left\lt -5,-6,2\right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,1\right>) \cdot \frac14 = (-7+2 - 3+2) \cdot \frac14=-1.5
